name: InfoGrid
tagline: Java 'web graph database' and REST app framework from NetMesh; abandoned, with source no longer online.
description: InfoGrid was an open-source Java platform sponsored by NetMesh Inc. and led by Johannes Ernst, pitched as a 'Web Graph Database'. Its core GraphDatabase stored typed MeshObjects and relationships; a Stores layer persisted them to SQL databases or distributed hashtables behind one API; a Grid project replicated graphs across many cooperating databases; and the Probe framework mapped external sources such as web feeds into the graph. On top sat REST-style URL mapping with 'Viewlets' for rendering objects, plus OpenID/LID identity support. It was AGPL v3 and active roughly 2008-2013. The code repository and Trac site are gone and infogrid.org shows only a placeholder, so it survives as history.
statusNote: No activity since about 2013; source and documentation are offline and infogrid.org shows a placeholder. Use Neo4j, JanusGraph or ArangoDB instead.

pricing.notes: AGPL open source with commercial support from NetMesh; nothing is offered today.

scale.notes: The Grid add-on replicated graphs across cooperating GraphDatabases.

strengths: Typed object graph with pluggable persistence to SQL or distributed stores
REST-style URLs and Viewlets made graph objects web-addressable
Probes imported external web data as graph objects
Replication protocol for federating many graph databases
weaknesses: Abandoned; source, docs and downloads are offline
No standard graph query language (pre-Cypher/Gremlin era API only)
useCases: History of early graph databases and linked-data web apps
notIdealFor: Any current project: the software is no longer available
